message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I don’t see a clear STEMI pattern on this image**, but this ECG alone cannot rule out a heart attack.

My tentative reading:

- Regular sinus rhythm, around **90–95 beats/min**, with narrow QRS complexes.
- Baseline drift and noise make ST-segment measurements less reliable.
- Mild ST–T changes, without convincing diagnostic ST elevation in neighboring leads.

If this is a current ECG with chest pain, breathlessness, sweating, nausea, or faintness, **call emergency services now and don’t drive yourself**. An initially nondiagnostic ECG can occur with acute coronary syndrome; assessment may require repeat ECGs and troponin blood tests. [ACC/AHA guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

What symptoms prompted the ECG, when did they start, and how old is the patient?
